notes.heading: Elements, compounds and mixtures
points: An element is made of one kind of atom and cannot be chemically broken into simpler substances.
A compound has atoms of different elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio, e.g. MgS or H2O.
A compound has new properties; H2O is not explosive and does not support combustion, unlike H2 and O2.
A mixture has two or more substances in no fixed ratio, not bonded, so each keeps its own properties.
Homogeneous mixtures are uniform throughout (air, sea water, alloys); heterogeneous ones are not (milk, paint, salad dressing).

notes.heading: Separating mixtures by physical methods
points: Dissolving: add solvent so the soluble substance dissolves and the insoluble one stays solid.
Filtration: liquid (filtrate) passes through the paper; insoluble solid stays behind as residue.
Evaporation or crystallization: heat off the solvent, or cool a hot solution, to get the dissolved solid back.
Distillation separates miscible liquids with different boiling points; the lower boiling one vaporizes first, then condenses in the condenser.
Paper chromatography: components with more affinity for the solvent (mobile phase) move faster than those held by the paper (stationary phase).

notes.heading: Kinetic molecular theory: states of matter
points: Solid: fixed shape and volume, strong attractions, particles vibrate in fixed positions, not compressible.
Liquid: fixed volume but no fixed shape, weaker attractions, particles vibrate, rotate and move around.
Gas: no fixed shape or volume, negligible attractions, particles move fastest, compressible.
State symbols: (s), (l), (g), and (aq) for dissolved in water.

notes.heading: Names of changes of state
points: Melting is solid to liquid; freezing is liquid to solid; vaporization (evaporation, boiling) is liquid to gas; condensation is gas to liquid.
Sublimation is solid straight to gas (dry ice); deposition is gas straight to solid (frost, snowflakes).
Melting, vaporization and sublimation absorb energy: endothermic.
Freezing, condensation and deposition release energy: exothermic; intermolecular forces get stronger.
During a change of state the temperature stays constant; the energy goes into overcoming forces between particles.

notes.heading: Temperature and the kelvin scale
points: Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of particles.
Kelvin temperature is proportional to average kinetic energy; Celsius is not.
A change of 1 K equals a change of 1 °C.
Convert with T(K) = T(°C) + 273.15; absolute zero is 0 K = −273.15 °C.
Kelvin is the SI base unit of temperature.

definitions.definition: A pure substance made of one kind of atom that cannot be chemically broken down into simpler substances.
definitions.trap: Saying an element is any pure substance; compounds are pure too.

definitions.definition: A pure substance of atoms of two or more different elements chemically bonded together in a fixed ratio.
definitions.trap: Calling a compound a mixture of its elements; it has new properties.

definitions.definition: Two or more elements or compounds not chemically bonded, in no fixed ratio, separable by physical methods.
definitions.trap: Forgetting that each component keeps its own properties.

definitions.definition: A mixture with uniform composition and properties throughout, with particles evenly distributed.
definitions.trap: Thinking uniform means pure; air and alloys are still mixtures.

definitions.definition: A mixture with non-uniform composition and varying properties, because particles are not evenly distributed.
The solution or liquid that passes through the filter paper during filtration.
definitions.trap: Mixing up filtrate (liquid through) with residue (solid left behind).

definitions.definition: The substance that remains after evaporation, distillation, filtration or a similar process.
A model in which matter is made of moving particles, explaining the properties of solids, liquids and gases and changes of state.
The change of state from solid directly to gas without passing through the liquid state.
definitions.trap: Confusing it with deposition, which is the reverse (gas to solid).

definitions.definition: The change of state from gas directly to solid, without becoming a liquid first.
definitions.trap: Calling it condensation, which is gas to liquid.

definitions.definition: A measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance.
definitions.trap: Saying it measures total energy or heat; it is the average.

definitions.definition: 0 K (−273.15 °C), the temperature at which particles cannot transfer any kinetic energy on collisions.
